message.content:
You are auditing token/BPE and "learned vs frozen" crystallization claims in /home/user/lance-graph for an architecture review. Report only what exists, with file:line citations. Never invent.

Tasks:
1. Find the real BPE / token carrier implementation. grep -ri "bpe\|byte.?pair" across lance-graph/crates/deepnsm, deepnsm-v2, thinking-engine, lance-graph-contract. What is the actual token representation (TokenId? WordId? bit width?)? Is BPE merging actually driven by position-mask co-occurrence (positions(A) AND SHIFT(positions(B)) style), or is it a conventional trained-vocabulary tokenizer (e.g. wrapping an existing BPE library)? Cite exact code.
2. Trie / vocabulary structure: grep -rli "trie\|vocabulary\|vocab" across lance-graph/crates/deepnsm-v2. Is there a real trie-addressable frozen structure, and is there any existing distinction in the code between "transient/active" state, "learned but revisable" state, and "frozen/compiled" state (three-tier)? Cite exact types/comments, or report NOT FOUND if this triangle doesn't exist yet.
3. Read tesseract-rs's CLAUDE.md section on "tesseract-paperless" and the "token" tier (search /home/user/tesseract-rs/CLAUDE.md for "seam_tantivy" / "ReceiptTokenizer" / "TokenLane") for the actual measured numbers on token-lane resident cost (the probe mentioned "Alice: 75513 B / 300 spans / 36994 tokens / 245 uniq / 55400 B resident" and "u8-vs-u16 rail" ratios). Confirm these numbers are real by finding the probe file if referenced, and report exactly what was measured (do not just copy from CLAUDE.md — note if you cannot independently verify against actual probe output).
4. Is there any existing "(tile, cell, port, token, delta)" event-shaped structure anywhere in the codebase, or would this be entirely new? grep -ri "tile.*cell.*port\|MergeEvent\|merge_event" across lance-graph/crates. Report FOUND (cite) or NOT FOUND.
5. Morton cascade in stamp probes: read crates/lance-graph-planner/examples/probe_stamp_morton_cascade.rs and probe_stamp_capacity.rs in full if they exist — what do they actually test, what numbers do they report in comments/output.

Output: structured report per question, exact file:line citations, exact numbers quoted with a note on their provenance (from a running probe vs from prose in a doc comment). Flag explicitly anything NOT FOUND.

8	//! **rung-2 meta-awareness** citizen: its subject matter is not the world but
9	//! the graph's own representation of the world.

11	//! ## Two detectors: [`detect_measured`] (shipped) vs [`detect`] (record)
12	//!
13	//! [`detect_measured`] is the SHIPPED router: it MEASURES the candidate trie

15	//! v1 STRUCTURAL router — it guessed shape from degree statistics and its

145	    entities.dedup();

148	    let max_out = out_deg.values().copied().max().unwrap_or(0);

157	    let cyclic = has_cycle(&entities, &adj);

3631	## ★ `tesseract-paperless` — document intake lands here, feature-gated (2026-08-24)
3632	
3633	Operator directive: *"can you add a paperless crate in Tesseract-rs instead and
3634	make it feature gated."* The work had been built in `AdaWorldAPI/paperless-rs`,
3635	whose push is denied at the GitHub-App level (403 through the session proxy AND
3636	proxy-bypassed; the in-environment `GH_TOKEN` is a 14-character placeholder, so
3637	the usual "a 403 here is the proxy" escape does not apply). It therefore had no
3638	durable home. **`crates/tesseract-paperless` is now the ONE source of truth**;
3639	the paperless-rs branch is a dead copy, archived as a patch under lance-graph
3640	`.claude/harvest/paperless-token-plateau/`. Do not sync the two — there is
3641	nothing to sync back to.
3642	
3643	### Why this does not breach the operator-set boundary
3644	
3645	This file already carries: *"tesseract-rs = faithful recognition → rich doc.v1
3646	… Store / graph / KV / PDF-from-data are NOT tesseract-rs concerns."* That rule
3647	stands, and three things keep the new crate on the right side of it:
3648	
3649	1. **It is a CONSUMER**, and this workspace already hosts consumers —
3650	   `tesseract-ocr-web`, `-pdf`, `-python`, `-ogar` are all downstream of
3651	   recognition rather than part of it.
3652	2. **No existing crate gains a dependency.** `tesseract-core`, `-recognizer`
3653	   and `-ocr` keep their exact dep sets. Recognition stays storage-less, which
3654	   is what the boundary actually protects.
3655	3. **There is no store.** `DedupIndex` is a trait and nothing here implements
3656	   it — the crate ships the GATE (a hash, a lookup contract, an ordering rule),
3657	   never the KV. That is the same line `OGAR-DOC-W4-BUILD-SPEC` draws: *"No
3658	   storage backend chosen (KV blob is the consumer's)."*
3659	
3660	### The three tiers, and why it is a MEMBER rather than excluded
3661	
3662	| tier | pulls | what it is |
3663	|---|---|---|
3664	| `default` | `sha2`, `lance-graph-contract`, `ogar-doc-ir`, `ogar-from-docv1` | the S-2 dedup gate + `doc.v1` → `DocIr` |
3665	| `ocr` | + `tesseract-ogar` | run the recognizer in-process |
3666	| `token` | + `tantivy`, `deepnsm-v2` | the lexical seam: one BPE tokenization per span, borrowed by several consumers |
3667	
3668	**Excluding it from the workspace would have been the wrong kind of gating.**
3669	An excluded crate is never compiled by CI, and an uncompiled crate rots
3670	invisibly — which this session watched happen for real to `spider_doc_ir`
3671	(a floating branch dep, no CI building the pair, broken for weeks by a field
3672	its own dependency added). A member with optional deps gets the opposite: the
3673	default build stays lean AND every tier has a CI line. All six lines are wired
3674	(`build`/`test`/`clippy` default, `clippy` ocr, `test`/`clippy` token) plus the
3675	probe itself, because the probe carries the evidence for every `token` claim.
3676	
3677	Note `token` turns on `lance-graph-contract/guid-v3-tail` transitively
3678	(deepnsm-v2 requires it, and requires it correctly — without it `mint_for`
3679	silently falls back to the V1 tail). Additive and correct, but it IS a
3680	graph-wide feature unification, so the manifest names it rather than leaving it
3681	to be discovered.
3682	
3683	### The DOM leg was replaced by something better, not dropped
3684	
3685	The paperless-rs version called `spider_doc_ir::harvest` directly, which both
3686	bound intake to one crawler and inherited its build — and that build is broken
3687	(`E0063: missing field 'confidence'`, a field `ogar-doc-ir` added after
3688	spider's only commit). The replacement is `ingest_doc_ir(bytes, index, build)`:
3689	the caller brings its own producer as a **closure**, so any producer that can
3690	build a `DocIr` is admitted and this crate depends on none of them. That is
3691	what a source-agnostic IR is FOR, and hard-coding one crawler had quietly spent
3692	the property.
3693	
3694	The closure — rather than an already-built `DocIr` — is what keeps S-2 true for
3695	a producer this crate has never heard of: on a duplicate it is **never called**.
3696	`a_duplicate_never_reaches_a_third_party_producer` proves it by passing a
3697	closure that PANICS, with the paired half proving the same closure DOES run on
3698	novel bytes (otherwise the first assertion would hold for a producer that is
3699	never called at all, which proves nothing about ordering).
3700	
3701	**One assertion was promoted to a runtime guard.** The old code merely *tested*
3702	that `spider_doc_ir`'s hash matched the gate's. `ingest_doc_ir` now REFUSES a
3703	mismatch (`IntakeError::IdentityMismatch`), because a producer that keys its IR
3704	by a normalised or re-encoded form of its input would otherwise leave the gate
3705	and the subtree silently addressing two different documents. Its falsifier uses
3706	exactly that realistic shape — a producer that hashes the trimmed input — and
3707	the paired half proves the guard is discriminating rather than always-on.
3708	
3709	### Evidence reproduced in the new home, not assumed
3710	
3711	The move is faithful, checked rather than trusted: `probe_token_seam` reports
3712	**ALL 41 GATES GREEN** with numbers identical to the paperless-rs run (Alice:
3713	75 513 B / 300 spans / 36 994 tokens / 245 uniq / 55 400 B resident), and both
3714	measurement probes reproduce (u8-vs-u16 rail: `alice-full` 1.95× cap-bound vs
3715	6.13× corpus-bound; WordId round-trips only 67.7 % of source bytes while
3716	TokenId is byte-exact). 13 lib tests, three tiers clippy-clean at
3717	`-D warnings`, fmt clean.
3718	
3719	Two things the move genuinely fixed rather than carried over: the whole
3720	`[patch]` section is **gone** (siblings are path deps here, which is this
3721	repo's convention, so the escaping-relative-path trap does not exist), and with
3722	it the branch-vs-rev unification problem — cargo does not unify a `branch` and
3723	a `rev` source even at the identical commit, and two SourceIds for
3724	`ogar-doc-ir` meant two incompatible `DocIr` types.
3725	
3726	### Disable table (both verified red-then-green)
3727	
3728	| assertion | disable | observed |
3729	|---|---|---|
3730	| a producer keyed by other bytes is refused | delete the `content_sha256 != hash` check | `a_producer_keyed_by_other_bytes_is_refused` FAILED |
3731	| a duplicate never reaches a third-party producer | move `build(source_bytes)` ahead of the short-circuit | `a_duplicate_never_reaches_a_third_party_producer` FAILED (the closure's own panic) |
3732	
3733	12 of 13 passed under each disable, so each one is pinned by exactly the test
3734	that names it rather than by collateral damage.
